tool.name: PlasBench aggregate
tool.description: per-sample scores into a ranked tool leaderboard
tool.command: ## aggregate_results.py writes <prefix>.leaderboard.tsv and friends, so give it ## a private working directory and collect the pieces Galaxy exposes. mkdir -p out && plasbench-aggregate --scores '$scores' #if $tool_status --tool-status '$tool_status' #end if --out-prefix out/benchmark && cp out/benchmark.leaderboard.tsv '$leaderboard' #if $emit_markdown && cp out/benchmark.leaderboard.md '$leaderboard_md' #end if

param.name: scores
param.label: Combined scores table
param.help: Rows from PlasBench score, concatenated across every sample and tool. One header row, then one row per sample/tool pair.

param.name: tool_status
param.label: Tool status table (optional)
param.help: Records which tool runs completed, were reused, skipped or failed. Supplying it lets the leaderboard distinguish a tool that scored badly from one that never ran.

param.name: emit_markdown
param.label: Also output the Markdown leaderboard
param.help: A formatted table for pasting into a report or slide.

tool.help:
**What it does**
Turns per-sample, per-tool score rows into a ranked leaderboard: mean and median F1, precision, base-level recall and plasmid-level recall for each tool, with bootstrap confidence intervals.
Stratified breakdowns (by organism, country, plasmid size, depth and AMR carriage) need the curated cohort sheet and are produced by the command-line pipeline rather than this wrapper.
**Read the intervals, not just the ranking.** With few samples the intervals overlap heavily, and two tools whose means look different may not be distinguishable at all. The leaderboard reports that rather than hiding it.
**Inputs**
Concatenate the tabular outputs of **PlasBench score** across every sample and tool — keeping a single header row — and supply the result here. The optional tool-status table lets the leaderboard separate "scored badly" from "never ran", which matters when a tool fails on some samples.
@METRIC_HELP@
